A Programming Paradigm for Spatiotemporal Composability

Abstract. We lift effects so that spatial and temporal composition share one algebra. The README page is HTML, not raw markdown, which is how GitHub renders a repository home when the raw artifact path is not used. The extractor must still recover the paper-shaped prose rather than repository chrome such as stars, forks, and file trees.

The core claim is that an effect signature can commute with a schedule. That sentence is easy to lose if a parser grabs the first sidebar article. This fixture therefore puts the real text in a semantic main and keeps the chrome in a complementary column so link density can drop it. Remaining words document the same idea with enough tokens to pass the default threshold on an English page.

Operators include sequence, par, and region. Sequence is time. Par is space. Region is the pair. Users write one expression and the runtime chooses a projection. Evidence comes from a small calculus and two implementations. Tradeoff: the algebra is stricter than ad-hoc promises, and the error messages are longer. Memory stays bounded because the schedule is explicit. Latency is the cost of the chosen projection, not a hidden queue.
